structured_output.summary:
In CompressedMaterialization::CompressComparisonJoin (src/optimizer/compressed_materialization/compress_comparison_join.cpp), I removed the block that compressed both columns of a single equality condition generically and added the probe key to probe_compress_bindings. Every condition now goes through GetReferencedBindings, so join keys are never compressed. Build-side payload columns are still compressed, and aggregate/order/distinct CM is unchanged.

Why it was slow: the hash join only builds a Bloom filter when `storage_offset.IsNull()` (physical_hash_join.cpp:1059). A probe key under a CM compress projection gets an offset, so its probe scan only got min/max filters and never the BF. With the change, q09's orders scan and q03's lineitem scan get the BF, as the profiles show.

Bench (4 runs, the bench itself is ±10-20% noisy): q09 -7.1%, -11.9%, -14.3%, -15.3%, -19.0%. q03 swung between +9.6% and -17% (-11.6% on the last full run). Last full bench geomean -4.8%, with nothing slower than +4.6% (q04).

The q19 "+21%" from early runs was noise. The q19 plan is identical with and without the change because CM never touches that join, and an unchanged tree measured -17% on q19. q13 still uses the perfect RIGHT HJ (0.39s for 15M probe rows) and measured -5.9..+3.9%. q18 was ±1.6%. I didn't try variant B (no join CM at all) because the key-only variant already gives the expected q09/q03 gains.
structured_output.generality: This helps any equality join whose probe key CM used to compress: integer FK joins whose build side passes the CM cardinality thresholds. Without the compress projection, the runtime BF (including the exact bitmap BF) reaches the probe table scan, and one compress/decompress pair per key goes away. Joins with several conditions, DELIM joins, and joins below the CM thresholds were never key-compressed and are unaffected. Possible downside: hash tables with very large builds keep 8-byte keys instead of 4-byte ones, which matters most for memory-bound or spilling joins. Payload compression, the part that matters most for memory, is kept. Correctness risk is minimal: uncompressed keys take the same path as joins below the CM thresholds.
structured_output.notes:
The bench is very noisy, ±20% per template on identical code (q19 and q08 especially), so compare profile plans before believing a regression.

On q13 the aggregate CM now adds a 15M-row compress projection (about 0.58s CPU) above the RIGHT join, replacing the old decompress/compress pair. Follow-up idea: skip the aggregate CM compress when the group key comes straight from a large join output and the perfect HA already uses the stats range.

An alternative fix would have been to let BF push through the storage_offset by shifting keys on the probe side. Removing key compression is simpler and also drops the projections.
